newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Switching Singapore mobile users can keep numbers.
newsitem.headline: Switching Singapore mobile users can keep numbers.

text.p: Mobile phone and pager users who switch to new operators when the Singapore market is liberalised next week can keep their existing numbers, the Telecommunication Authority of Singapore (TAS) said on Tuesday.

TAS said in a statement it had agreed with the current monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel), and all the new competitors on systems for transferring calls and messages between services if necessary.
Mobile phone calls would be exchanged through a call-forwarding system while paging messages would be transfered using SingTel's Automatic Interception Service (AIS).
"This number portability will be offered by all operators to mobile phone and paging users from April 1, 1997," TAS said.
It said charges for switching ranged from Singapore $8-10 per month, a level which TAS considered to be fair.
From April 1, SingTel will face one competitor, MobileOne, in the Singapore mobile phone market and three new entrants in the pager market.
MobileOne is a joint venture of Britain's Cable & Wireless, Hong Kong Telecommunications, Keppel Telecom and Singapore Press Holdings.
The new paging companies are MobileOne, state-owned ST Messaging and Hutchison Paging, a joint venture of Hutchison Whampoa Ltd of Hong Kong and Singapore conglomerate Intraco Ltd.
